headline: Budget panel hears Environmental Management plan and sewer rate increase

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.voteItem: Closing public testimony and accepting written testimony on BFED 1
meeting.summary: The budget committee heard the Environmental Management budget plan, including a 9% sewer rate increase, and closed public testimony.
meeting.recap: The Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee met April 16, 2026, with the vice chair acting as chair.[[0:06:00]] The only agenda item was the County's proposed fiscal year 2027 budget.[[0:08:35]] A council member reported that 28 people testified at a South Maui budget meeting.[[0:09:03]] Another council member reported that 10 people testified at an April 15 budget meeting on Lānaʻi.[[0:12:35]] The department asked for $1.25 million more in grants than in fiscal year 26.[[0:20:44]] It proposed a 9% average increase in wastewater (sewer) rates, bringing in about $2.2 million more.[[0:24:45]] Monthly trash pickup fees would rise $1 on Maui and Molokaʻi, from $36 to $37.[[0:25:37]] A watershed group said it is seeking up to $600,000 to create five new positions.[[0:58:22]] A Haʻikū group asked to restore $40,000 for a fourth year of stream testing.[[1:31:27]] The committee closed public testimony with no objections.[[1:52:24]] The recording ends as the vice chair asks whether members object to a recess.[[1:56:49]]
decided: The committee closed public testimony and accepted written testimony with no objections.
meeting.next: The vice chair said Member Johnson would start questions when the committee returns from recess. The watershed group's executive director agreed to submit a map of the proposed work area.

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: A Haʻikū resident testified about a planned test well that is partly meant to meet a 2003 consent decree (a court-approved agreement).
issues.why: The resident said the well must be done correctly so the aquifer (underground water supply) is not overcommitted.
issues.brief: The resident said the Department of Water Supply will not drill a deep monitoring well for the aquifer.[[#1]] A Haʻikū community group asked to restore $40,000 for a fourth year of stream testing.[[#2]] A watershed group leader said the full cloud bridge restoration initiative is slated for about $2.9 million.[[#3]]
